name: Space-time white noise
description: A Gaussian generalized random field on R+ x R^d whose values over disjoint space-time regions are independent with covariance equal to the Lebesgue measure of their overlap.
source_article: Some recent progress in singular stochastic PDEs, Ivan Corwin and Hao Shen, 2020 (BAMS 57:409-454)

name: Linear stochastic heat equation with additive noise
description: The SPDE d_t u = d_x^2 u + xi driven by space-time white noise, whose solution is almost surely Holder C^alpha for alpha < (2-d)/2 and hence distribution-valued for d >= 2.
source_article: Some recent progress in singular stochastic PDEs, Ivan Corwin and Hao Shen, 2020 (BAMS 57:409-454)

name: Dynamical Phi^4 equation
description: The renormalized stochastic reaction-diffusion equation d_t Phi = Delta Phi - (Phi^3 - infinity*Phi) + xi, the Langevin dynamics of the Phi^4 Euclidean quantum field theory, which is singular for spatial dimension d = 2,3.
source_article: Some recent progress in singular stochastic PDEs, Ivan Corwin and Hao Shen, 2020 (BAMS 57:409-454)

name: KPZ equation
description: The Kardar-Parisi-Zhang stochastic PDE d_t H = d_x^2 H + (d_x H)^2 + xi modeling random interface growth, singular because (d_x H)^2 multiplies distribution-valued objects.
source_article: Some recent progress in singular stochastic PDEs, Ivan Corwin and Hao Shen, 2020 (BAMS 57:409-454)

name: Parabolic Anderson Model
description: The linear singular SPDE d_t u = Delta u + u*(zeta - infinity) with spatial white noise potential zeta, requiring renormalization in dimension d >= 2.
source_article: Some recent progress in singular stochastic PDEs, Ivan Corwin and Hao Shen, 2020 (BAMS 57:409-454)

name: Renormalization (counter-term subtraction) for singular SPDEs
description: The procedure of mollifying the noise, subtracting divergent counter-terms C_epsilon (chosen via explicit Gaussian moment/Wick-power computations) from the nonlinearity, and passing to the limit to obtain a nontrivial solution.
source_article: Some recent progress in singular stochastic PDEs, Ivan Corwin and Hao Shen, 2020 (BAMS 57:409-454)

name: Da Prato-Debussche trick
description: A solution method that splits the solution Phi = u + v into the stochastic linear (Gaussian) part u and a remainder v of higher regularity satisfying a classically well-posed fixed-point equation, valid for 'not too singular' equations such as 2D Phi^4.
source_article: Some recent progress in singular stochastic PDEs, Ivan Corwin and Hao Shen, 2020 (BAMS 57:409-454)

name: Theory of regularity structures
description: Hairer's framework that builds a local algebraic-analytic expansion of solutions in terms of a hierarchy of explicit stochastic objects (a model and modelled distributions), yielding well-posedness for the most singular subcritical SPDEs such as 3D Phi^4 and KPZ.
source_article: Some recent progress in singular stochastic PDEs, Ivan Corwin and Hao Shen, 2020 (BAMS 57:409-454)

name: Paracontrolled distributions
description: The Gubinelli-Imkeller-Perkowski method that controls the solution by expressing it as a paraproduct against a fixed reference distribution, providing an alternative to regularity structures for singular SPDEs.
source_article: Some recent progress in singular stochastic PDEs, Ivan Corwin and Hao Shen, 2020 (BAMS 57:409-454)

name: KPZ universality
description: The conjectured/established principle that the KPZ equation and Tracy-Widom-type fluctuations arise as universal scaling limits of a wide class of microscopic growth and interacting particle systems (e.g. ASEP, six-vertex model, solid-on-solid model).
source_article: Some recent progress in singular stochastic PDEs, Ivan Corwin and Hao Shen, 2020 (BAMS 57:409-454)

name: Primary uncertainty principle
description: For linear operators A, B with ||A||_{1->inf} <= 1, ||B||_{1->inf} <= 1 and ||BAv||_inf >= k||v||_inf, one has ||v||_1 ||Av||_1 >= k ||v||_inf ||Av||_inf, a one-line inequality from which classical Fourier uncertainty principles follow.
source_article: The uncertainty principle: variations on a theme, Avi Wigderson and Yuval Wigderson, 2021 (BAMS 58:225-261)

name: k-Hadamard matrix
description: A matrix A all of whose entries are bounded by 1 in absolute value and satisfying ||A*Av||_inf >= k||v||_inf, equivalently A*A invertible with ||(A*A)^{-1}||_{inf->inf} <= 1/k; precisely the matrices to which the primary uncertainty principle applies.
source_article: The uncertainty principle: variations on a theme, Avi Wigderson and Yuval Wigderson, 2021 (BAMS 58:225-261)

name: Heisenberg uncertainty principle
description: The variance of a function and the variance of its Fourier transform cannot both be small, i.e. integral |x|^2|f|^2 times integral |xi|^2|fhat|^2 >= ||f||_2^4/4, with equality for Gaussians.
source_article: The uncertainty principle: variations on a theme, Avi Wigderson and Yuval Wigderson, 2021 (BAMS 58:225-261)

name: Donoho-Stark support-size uncertainty principle
description: For a nonzero function f on a finite abelian group G with Fourier transform fhat, the supports satisfy |supp(f)|*|supp(fhat)| >= |G|.
dependencies: Fourier transform on finite abelian groups
source_article: The uncertainty principle: variations on a theme, Avi Wigderson and Yuval Wigderson, 2021 (BAMS 58:225-261)

name: Meshulam's non-abelian uncertainty principle
description: An extension of the Donoho-Stark support-size inequality to functions on arbitrary (non-abelian) finite groups via rank and min-support notions of support for the Fourier transform.
source_article: The uncertainty principle: variations on a theme, Avi Wigderson and Yuval Wigderson, 2021 (BAMS 58:225-261)

name: Hardy's uncertainty principle
description: If |f(x)| <= C e^{-a|x|^2} and |fhat(xi)| <= C e^{-b|xi|^2} with ab > 1/4 then f = 0, and with ab = 1/4 then f is a constant multiple of the Gaussian e^{-a|x|^2}.
source_article: Dynamical versions of Hardy's uncertainty principle: A survey, Aingeru Fernandez-Bertolin and Eugenia Malinnikova, 2021 (BAMS 58:357-375)

name: Dynamical (Schrodinger) reformulation of Hardy's uncertainty principle
description: The reinterpretation of Hardy's theorem as a unique-continuation/rigidity statement for solutions of the free Schrodinger equation: a solution Gaussian-bounded at two distinct times must vanish, equating Fourier decay with two-time evolution decay.
source_article: Dynamical versions of Hardy's uncertainty principle: A survey, Aingeru Fernandez-Bertolin and Eugenia Malinnikova, 2021 (BAMS 58:357-375)

name: Liouville-theorem proof of Hardy's uncertainty principle
description: A proof (reviving Hardy's forgotten second argument) deriving the uncertainty principle from the Schrodinger connection together with Liouville's theorem for bounded entire functions rather than Phragmen-Lindelof.
dependencies: dynamical (Schrodinger) reformulation of Hardy's uncertainty principle
source_article: Dynamical versions of Hardy's uncertainty principle: A survey, Aingeru Fernandez-Bertolin and Eugenia Malinnikova, 2021 (BAMS 58:357-375)

name: Sine-kernel Fredholm determinant
description: The determinant P_x = det(1 - K_sine) of the trace-class operator on L^2(J) with kernel sin(x(z-z'))/(pi(z-z')), giving the probability of no GUE eigenvalues in a union of intervals in the bulk scaling limit.
source_article: Harold Widom's work in random matrix theory, Ivan Corwin, Percy Deift and Alexander Its, 2022 (BAMS 59:155-173)

name: Widom's large-gap asymptotics for the sine-kernel determinant
description: Widom's rigorous proof that ln P_x = -(x^2/2)(1 + o(1)) (and d/dx ln P_x = -x + O(1)) as x -> infinity, the first rigorous large-gap asymptotics for the sine determinant.
source_article: Harold Widom's work in random matrix theory, Ivan Corwin, Percy Deift and Alexander Its, 2022 (BAMS 59:155-173)

name: Tracy-Widom distribution functions
description: The limiting distributions F_beta(t) (beta = 1,2,4) of the largest eigenvalue of large GOE/GUE/GSE matrices after edge rescaling, with F_2(t) = det(1 - K_Airy) given by the Airy-kernel Fredholm determinant.
source_article: Harold Widom's work in random matrix theory, Ivan Corwin, Percy Deift and Alexander Its, 2022 (BAMS 59:155-173)

name: Tracy-Widom Painleve representation
description: The identity F_2(t) = exp(-integral_t^infty (s-t)u(s)^2 ds) where u is the Hastings-McLeod solution of the second Painleve equation u_tt = t u + 2u^3, with F_1 and F_4 expressed through u as well.
source_article: Harold Widom's work in random matrix theory, Ivan Corwin, Percy Deift and Alexander Its, 2022 (BAMS 59:155-173)

name: Integrable Fredholm operator
description: An integral operator on L^2(J) whose kernel has the form (phi(z)psi(z')-psi(z)phi(z'))/(z-z') (sum of f_j(z)h_j(z')), a structure whose determinant satisfies nonlinear integrable PDEs and admits a Riemann-Hilbert representation.
source_article: Harold Widom's work in random matrix theory, Ivan Corwin, Percy Deift and Alexander Its, 2022 (BAMS 59:155-173)

name: Riemann-Hilbert / nonlinear steepest descent method
description: The representation of Painleve and integrable-determinant functions as solutions of matrix Riemann-Hilbert problems, whose asymptotics (including connection formulae) are computed via the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent deformation of contours.
source_article: Harold Widom's work in random matrix theory, Ivan Corwin, Percy Deift and Alexander Its, 2022 (BAMS 59:155-173)

name: Arnold's geodesic formulation of ideal hydrodynamics
description: The principle that the incompressible Euler equations are the geodesic equations of the right-invariant L^2 (kinetic-energy) metric on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of the fluid domain.
source_article: Geometric hydrodynamics and infinite-dimensional Newton's equations, Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek and Klas Modin, 2021 (BAMS 58:377-442)

name: Newton's equations on diffeomorphism groups and density spaces
description: The generalization grad_dot(q) dot(q) = -grad U(q) of the geodesic flow to infinite dimensions, with a potential U on Diff(M) or Dens(M), unifying compressible/incompressible fluids, MHD, shallow-water and relativistic fluid equations.
dependencies: Arnold's geodesic formulation of ideal hydrodynamics
source_article: Geometric hydrodynamics and infinite-dimensional Newton's equations, Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek and Klas Modin, 2021 (BAMS 58:377-442)

name: Wasserstein-Otto metric on densities
description: The optimal-transport (L^2 Wasserstein) Riemannian metric on the space of probability densities, realized as a Riemannian submersion image of the L^2 metric on the full diffeomorphism group.
source_article: Geometric hydrodynamics and infinite-dimensional Newton's equations, Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek and Klas Modin, 2021 (BAMS 58:377-442)

name: Fisher-Rao information metric (infinite-dimensional)
description: The information-geometric Riemannian metric on probability densities invariant under diffeomorphisms, used as the base geometry whose Newton equations yield the mu-Camassa-Holm and Klein-Gordon type equations.
source_article: Geometric hydrodynamics and infinite-dimensional Newton's equations, Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek and Klas Modin, 2021 (BAMS 58:377-442)

name: Madelung transform as a symplectomorphism
description: The map sending a wave function to its density-and-phase (hydrodynamic) variables is a symplectomorphism (and Kahler morphism) intertwining the Schrodinger equation with Newton's equations of compressible fluids on the space of densities.
source_article: Geometric hydrodynamics and infinite-dimensional Newton's equations, Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek and Klas Modin, 2021 (BAMS 58:377-442)

name: Symplectic and Poisson reduction for hydrodynamics
description: The reduction of Hamiltonian systems with symmetry (semidirect-product groups) used to derive the Hamiltonian/Poisson structures, Casimir invariants, and equations of motion for ideal, barotropic and magneto-hydrodynamic fluids.
dependencies: Newton's equations on diffeomorphism groups and density spaces
source_article: Geometric hydrodynamics and infinite-dimensional Newton's equations, Boris Khesin, Gerard Misiolek and Klas Modin, 2021 (BAMS 58:377-442)

name: Hadamard well-posedness
description: The standard requiring, for an evolution problem in a Sobolev scale H^s, existence of a solution in C([0,T];H^s), uniqueness in that class, and continuous dependence of the solution on the initial data.
source_article: Local well-posedness for quasilinear problems: a primer, Mihaela Ifrim and Daniel Tataru, 2023 (BAMS 60:167-194)

name: Frequency envelopes
description: A device assigning a slowly varying admissible sequence dominating the Littlewood-Paley pieces of the data, used to track and propagate the dyadic distribution of energy and thereby prove continuous dependence and rough-data well-posedness.
source_article: Local well-posedness for quasilinear problems: a primer, Mihaela Ifrim and Daniel Tataru, 2023 (BAMS 60:167-194)

name: Rough solutions as limits of smooth solutions
description: The roadmap that constructs low-regularity solutions of quasilinear evolutions by regularizing the data, solving smoothly, and passing to the limit using uniform energy and frequency-envelope bounds, yielding existence, uniqueness and continuous dependence in one scheme.
source_article: Local well-posedness for quasilinear problems: a primer, Mihaela Ifrim and Daniel Tataru, 2023 (BAMS 60:167-194)

name: Quasilinear energy estimates
description: Coercive a priori bounds for symmetric (or symmetrizable) hyperbolic systems d_t u = A_j(u)d_j u obtained by differentiating, symmetrizing and integrating by parts, controlling the H^s norm in terms of a lower (Lipschitz) norm of the solution.
source_article: Local well-posedness for quasilinear problems: a primer, Mihaela Ifrim and Daniel Tataru, 2023 (BAMS 60:167-194)

name: Convex integration in hydrodynamics
description: An iterative construction adding high-frequency oscillatory perturbations (e.g. Mikado/intermittent flows) to approximate solutions of the fluid equations so as to cancel a Reynolds stress error in the limit, producing wild weak solutions.
source_article: Convex integration constructions in hydrodynamics, Tristan Buckmaster and Vlad Vicol, 2021 (BAMS 58:1-44)

name: Onsager's conjecture
description: The conjecture that weak solutions of the incompressible Euler equations conserve kinetic energy if their Holder regularity exponent exceeds 1/3 and may dissipate it below 1/3.
source_article: Convex integration constructions in hydrodynamics, Tristan Buckmaster and Vlad Vicol, 2021 (BAMS 58:1-44)

name: Resolution of the flexible side of Onsager's conjecture
description: The construction (Isett; Buckmaster-De Lellis-Szekelyhidi-Vicol) via convex integration of C^{1/3-} weak solutions of the Euler equations that dissipate energy, proving the sharp threshold predicted by Onsager.
source_article: Convex integration constructions in hydrodynamics, Tristan Buckmaster and Vlad Vicol, 2021 (BAMS 58:1-44)

name: Nonuniqueness of weak solutions of Navier-Stokes
description: Buckmaster-Vicol's theorem that the 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations admit nonunique weak solutions with bounded kinetic energy, obtained by intermittent convex integration.
source_article: Convex integration constructions in hydrodynamics, Tristan Buckmaster and Vlad Vicol, 2021 (BAMS 58:1-44)

name: Intermittency in convex integration
description: The use of spatially concentrated (high L^infinity, low L^p for p<2) building-block flows that mimic turbulent energy concentration and supply the extra integrability needed to dissipate viscosity in Navier-Stokes constructions.
source_article: Convex integration constructions in hydrodynamics, Tristan Buckmaster and Vlad Vicol, 2021 (BAMS 58:1-44)

name: Polya-Fourier transform with Gaussian factor
description: The entire function H_{rho,lambda}(z) = integral e^{izt} e^{lambda t^2} drho(t) extending the Riemann xi-function, whose real-zeros property as lambda varies encodes the Riemann Hypothesis.
source_article: Constants of de Bruijn-Newman type in analytic number theory and statistical physics, Charles Newman and Wei Wu, 2019 (BAMS 57:595-614)

name: de Bruijn-Newman constant
description: The finite constant Lambda_DN in (-infinity, 1/2] such that H_{Phi,lambda} has only real zeros iff lambda >= Lambda_DN, so that the Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to Lambda_DN <= 0.
source_article: Constants of de Bruijn-Newman type in analytic number theory and statistical physics, Charles Newman and Wei Wu, 2019 (BAMS 57:595-614)

name: Polya monotonicity / De Bruijn upper bound / Newman lower bound
description: The three facts that the real-zeros set P_Phi is an upper half-line (Polya), contains 1/2 (De Bruijn), and is bounded below (Newman), which together define Lambda_DN.
source_article: Constants of de Bruijn-Newman type in analytic number theory and statistical physics, Charles Newman and Wei Wu, 2019 (BAMS 57:595-614)

name: Rodgers-Tao theorem (Lambda_DN >= 0)
description: The 2018 proof by Rodgers and Tao of Newman's 1976 conjecture that the de Bruijn-Newman constant is nonnegative, formalizing that the Riemann Hypothesis, if true, is only barely so.
source_article: Constants of de Bruijn-Newman type in analytic number theory and statistical physics, Charles Newman and Wei Wu, 2019 (BAMS 57:595-614)

name: Newman-Wu weak-convergence theorem for real-zero distributions
description: A theorem that the purely-real-zeros property of Fourier transforms of a sequence of probability measures controls their tail behavior uniformly, used to classify the joint behavior of (T_rho, P_rho).
source_article: Constants of de Bruijn-Newman type in analytic number theory and statistical physics, Charles Newman and Wei Wu, 2019 (BAMS 57:595-614)

name: Euler alignment (hydrodynamic alignment) equations
description: The pressure-augmented continuity-momentum system d_t rho + div(rho u) = 0, d_t(rho u) + div(rho u tensor u + P) = A(rho,u) with nonlocal alignment forcing A weighted by a symmetric communication kernel phi.
source_article: Swarming: hydrodynamic alignment with pressure, Eitan Tadmor, 2023 (BAMS 60:285-325)

name: p-alignment hydrodynamics
description: The class of alignment models based on (fractional) weighted 2p-graph Laplacians, generalizing Cucker-Smale alignment to nonlinear p-Laplacian-type interaction operators.
source_article: Swarming: hydrodynamic alignment with pressure, Eitan Tadmor, 2023 (BAMS 60:285-325)

name: Entropic pressure tensor
description: A pressure law required only to form an energy-dissipative process (no thermodynamic closure assumption), introduced to study long-time alignment dynamics with general pressure.
source_article: Swarming: hydrodynamic alignment with pressure, Eitan Tadmor, 2023 (BAMS 60:285-325)

name: Flocking of p-alignment with entropic pressure
description: Tadmor's result that p-alignment hydrodynamics driven by singular (heavy-tailed) communication kernels flock unconditionally even with general entropic pressure tensors and no closure assumption.
source_article: Swarming: hydrodynamic alignment with pressure, Eitan Tadmor, 2023 (BAMS 60:285-325)

name: Energy-fluctuation decay method for flocking
description: The strategy of quantifying flocking by controlling the decay of velocity-energy fluctuations, with enstrophy bounds upgraded to Holder regularity and uniform dispersion bounds, to prove emergence under heavy-tailed kernels.
dependencies: flocking of p-alignment with entropic pressure
source_article: Swarming: hydrodynamic alignment with pressure, Eitan Tadmor, 2023 (BAMS 60:285-325)

name: Non-Euclidean (incompatible) elasticity
description: The variational model in which a growing thin body carries a prescribed target metric g that is generally not realizable by an isometric immersion, and the observed shape minimizes an elastic energy measuring deviation of the realized metric from g.
source_article: Geometry, analysis, and morphogenesis: Problems and prospects, Marta Lewicka and L. Mahadevan, 2022 (BAMS 59:331-369)

name: Metric frustration as the origin of biological shape
description: The principle that morphogenesis of thin tissues results from differential growth inducing an incompatible (e.g. hyperbolic) metric whose frustrated embedding into R^3 selects a shape by elastic energy minimization.
source_article: Geometry, analysis, and morphogenesis: Problems and prospects, Marta Lewicka and L. Mahadevan, 2022 (BAMS 59:331-369)

name: Gamma-convergence hierarchy of thin elastic plate/shell theories
description: The derivation, as the (scaled) thickness tends to zero, of a hierarchy of reduced 2D energies (membrane, von Karman, bending/Kirchhoff) as Gamma-limits of 3D non-Euclidean elastic energies, indexed by the scaling exponent of the energy.
source_article: Geometry, analysis, and morphogenesis: Problems and prospects, Marta Lewicka and L. Mahadevan, 2022 (BAMS 59:331-369)

name: Convex-integration construction of low-regularity isometric immersions of prestrained films
description: The use of Nash-Kuiper-type convex integration to construct C^{1,alpha} very-weak (non-Euclidean) isometric immersions realizing prescribed growth metrics, with energy-scaling estimates for the resulting frustrated shapes.
dependencies: metric frustration as the origin of biological shape
source_article: Geometry, analysis, and morphogenesis: Problems and prospects, Marta Lewicka and L. Mahadevan, 2022 (BAMS 59:331-369)

name: Monge-Ampere constrained energy for weak prestrains
description: The reduced energy governing weakly prestrained thin films whose admissible out-of-plane deflections are constrained by a Monge-Ampere (Gauss-curvature) equation det(D^2 v) = f.
dependencies: Gamma-convergence hierarchy of thin elastic plate/shell theories
source_article: Geometry, analysis, and morphogenesis: Problems and prospects, Marta Lewicka and L. Mahadevan, 2022 (BAMS 59:331-369)

name: Boolean / Gaussian noise stability
description: The probability that two rho-correlated random inputs (on the discrete cube or, in the Gaussian limit, on R^n) yield the same output of a function, the central quantity governing probabilistic social-choice results.
source_article: Probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Elchanan Mossel, 2022 (BAMS 59:297-330)

name: Majority is Stablest theorem
description: Among balanced Boolean functions with vanishingly small individual influences, the majority function maximizes noise stability, with the optimal value given by a Gaussian (arccos) formula.
source_article: Probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Elchanan Mossel, 2022 (BAMS 59:297-330)

name: Gaussian (quantitative) Arrow theorem
description: A quantitative version of Arrow's impossibility theorem stating that any near-rational social welfare aggregation rule with small influences must be close to a dictatorship, with the probability of a non-rational (paradoxical) outcome bounded below.
source_article: Probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Elchanan Mossel, 2022 (BAMS 59:297-330)

name: Quantitative Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem
description: A robust version of the Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem: any social choice function far from dictatorship has a non-negligible probability of being manipulable by a random voter, proved via isoperimetric arguments on the rankings graph.
source_article: Probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Elchanan Mossel, 2022 (BAMS 59:297-330)

name: Invariance principle for low-influence functions
description: A nonlinear Lindeberg-type theorem showing that low-degree, low-influence multilinear polynomials have nearly the same distribution under Bernoulli and Gaussian inputs, the key device reducing discrete voting problems to Gaussian geometry.
source_article: Probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Elchanan Mossel, 2022 (BAMS 59:297-330)

name: KKL (Kahn-Kalai-Linial) influence theorem
description: Every balanced Boolean function on n variables has a coordinate with influence at least Omega(log n / n), establishing that some voter must be relatively influential.
source_article: Probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Elchanan Mossel, 2022 (BAMS 59:297-330)
